events.title: Yoga
events.category: Outdoor Fitness | Exercise Classes | Yoga & Pilates Classes
events.description: Start your morning off balanced and refreshed with a free yoga class led by local yoga instructors Mariah and Frances in Garibaldi Plaza. Bring a yoga mat and water bottle.

events.title: Cardio Sculpt
events.category: Fitness | Shape Up NYC | Outdoor Fitness | Exercise Classes
events.description: This cardio workout consists of functional movement exercises designed to make daily activities easier to perform. Meets at the athletic courts.

events.title: Zumba Gold®

sourcePlace.name: Constance Baker Motley Recreation Center
sourcePlace.address: Dance Room (in Constance Baker Motley Recreation Center)

events.category: Dance | Fitness | Shape Up NYC | Recreation Center Programming | Dance Classes | Exercise Classes
events.description: Zumba Gold® offers a low-impact workout set to a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes, creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system! The routines feature aerobic fitness interval training with a combination of fast and slow rhythms that challenge both the heart and muscles. With fun music and easy-to-follow steps, you can’t go wrong! Participants must sign in at the front desk and bring locks to lock up their bags. The center does not allow anyone to bring their bags to the dance room except: towel, water and phone.

events.title: Soundview Park Forest Restoration

sourcePlace.name: Soundview Park
sourcePlace.address: Lacombe Ave & Rosedale Ave (in Soundview Park)

events.description: Volunteer with the Stewardship team to protect the forested areas in Soundview Park! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been funded in part by NYC Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to [email omitted].

events.title: Forest Fridays: Volunteer Forest Restoration at Van Cortlandt Park

sourcePlace.name: Van Cortlandt Park
sourcePlace.address: Van Cortlandt Classic Playground (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.description: Join the Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for forest restoration along the southern section of the Old Croton Aqueduct Trail. We remove invasive bush honeysuckle and multiflora rose by hand so native trees, shrubs and wildflowers can come back.Dates include Fridays weekly from October 2nd - October 30th. Dates are 10/2, 10/9, 10/16, 10/23, and 10/30.Meeting Details:Location: Classic Playground, Van Cortlandt Park South and Gouverneur Avenue. events.title: Farm Stand
events.description: Come to Powell Street Garden and see what the garden group grew for the community at their farm stand! The farm stand is also hosted on October 3, 9, 10, 16,17, 23, 24, 30, and 31.

events.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
events.description: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova. Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

events.title: Low Impact Dance Fitness
events.category: Dance | Fitness | Shape Up NYC | Recreation Center Programming | Dance Classes | Exercise Classes
events.description: This fun, low-impact dance fitness class is designed to make you feel energized! Here, we focus on cardio and full-body movements to give you a well-rounded workout. Come join us!

events.title: Running Group
events.category: Fitness | Shape Up NYC | Outdoor Fitness | Exercise Classes | Running/Jogging
events.description: This welcoming, beginner-friendly running group uses walk/run intervals to help you gradually build your endurance and confidence. Each session increases the running time at a comfortable pace, helping you progress step by step toward completing a 5K.

events.category: Fitness | Shape Up NYC | Recreation Center Programming | Exercise Classes | Yoga & Pilates Classes
events.description: Conéctate, equilibra y desafíate con Yoga en español. events.description: The Kids in Motion program engages children in active, outdoors play. A NYC Parks staff member leads four to seven hours of free activities in NYC's playgrounds, including organized sports, games, fitness demos, board games, and more!Kids in Motion is a free, drop-in program without registration. Children can head to the playground during the listed hours of operation to participate. Occasionally a kids in Motion program may be cancelled due to harsh weather or other conditions. events.title: Proximity Exhibition

events.description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another. events.title: The History of the Ouija Board

sourcePlace.name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
sourcePlace.address: Visitor Information Booth (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)

events.description: Dive into the history of the enigmatic Ouija board, and learn how spirit communication became a phenomenon that swept the nation. Today a trademarked game owned and manufactured by Hasbro, Ouija has a history that stretches back to the 19th century. At one time, the "talking board" outsold Monopoly—appearing in silent films, Valentine's Day greeting cards, popular sheet music, and even a Norman Rockwell illustration. Get an up-close look at more than a dozen vintage boards—all with their own unique design and aesthetic—that have dazzled the curious and mystified skeptics for more than one hundred years. events.description: Join the Open House New York 2026 Festival and explore the grounds of the Historic Brougham Cottage in Blue Heron Park!Located at 4746 Amboy Road, Staten Island, NY, and located within a wooded backdrop, the circa 1726 Brougham Cottage is a surviving Dutch H-frame home.Brougham Cottage survives as a rare example of the small vernacular farm houses that were once common in the 18th and early 19th century rural landscape and have all but disappeared. events.description: Chester Commodore was one of the most influential and acclaimed African American cartoonists of the twentieth century. During the nearly 50 years his cartoons appeared in the Chicago Defender, Commodore used his art to advocate for racial justice, human rights, and equality of opportunity. events.description: Diddley Bow Archives Tie: The Black Ensemble Theater Company Records Collection Chicago has a rich heritage of internationally renowned electric blues guitar players, such as Muddy Waters, Elmore James, Buddy Guy and many more. This workshop elevates this Chicago history by exploring the rise of the electric blues and some of its musicians’ very first musical instrument, the diddley bow, a one-stringed instrument sometimes also referred to as a cigar box guitar. events.title: Chicago's Electric Blues Heritage and History: Diddley Bow Workshop
events.category: Chicago 250 | Crafts, Games and Play | Workshops
events.description: Diddley Bow Archives Tie: The Black Ensemble Theater Company Records Collection Chicago has a rich heritage of internationally renowned electric blues guitar players, such as Muddy Waters, Elmore James, Buddy Guy and many more. This workshop elevates this Chicago history by exploring the rise of the electric blues and some of its musicians’ very first musical instrument, the diddley bow, a one-stringed instrument sometimes also referred to as a cigar box guitar. Inspired by the history of Chicago’s renowned blues guitarists extracted from CPL’s archives, participants will build their own cigar box guitar. Musician Coco Elysses will present the diddley bow’s history, demonstrate its sound, and then instruct on how to build the instrument. Supplies will be provided. The program runs about 1.

Every Tuesday! Whether you’ve never touched a chess piece or you’ve loved the game for years, this hour is for you! We’ll learn together, practice together, and enjoy thoughtful play in a friendly, welcoming space. Chess is more than a game — it’s a way to slow down, think creatively, and connect with others. During the Hour You Can: · Learn the basics at your own pace · Practice with other players · Explore fun strategies and puzzles · Ask questions in a supportive setting · Meet new people through shared play Whether you’ve never touched a chess piece or you’ve loved the game for years, this hour is for you! During his acclaimed 60-year career, he was a significant creator of public art in Chicago and across the U.S., with 160 public sculpture commissions in 24 states that included monuments of several notable figures. Create your own mixed-media sculptures using clay, wire, cardboard, aluminum foil, and paint, inspired by Hunt’s abstract forms and his ability to transform metal into movement. Art activities may include: Modular Sculptures: Using geometric shapes and layering to build height and form. Figura

events.description: From 1976 to 1987 artist Calvin B. Jones along with fellow artist Mitchell Canton painted six murals on the South and West sides of Chicago. events.title: Sculpt Like Hunt and Perkins: A Creative Sculpting Workshop
events.description: This workshop highlights the accomplishments of Black Chicago sculptors with a spotlight on Richard Hunt and Marion Perkins. Hunt, a world-renowned sculptor and printmaker born in Chicago’s Woodlawn community and raised in Englewood, became one of the leading 20th century American artists. During his acclaimed 60-year career, he was a significant creator of public art in Chicago and across the U.S., with 160 public sculpture commissions in 24 states that included monuments of several notable figures. Create your own mixed-media sculptures using clay, wire, cardboard, aluminum foil, and paint, inspired by Hunt’s abstract forms and his ability to transform metal into movement. events.title: Meet Chester Commodore: Drawing and Illustration 101
events.description: Chester Commodore was one of the most influential and acclaimed African American cartoonists of the twentieth century. During the nearly 50 years his cartoons appeared in the Chicago Defender, Commodore used his art to advocate for racial justice, human rights, and equality of opportunity. From the 1954 appearance of his world-famous first editorial cartoon (on the Supreme Court’s Brown v. Board of Education, featuring a hammer breaking chains); his work reached an international audience. More than that, his widely seen cartoons helped to bridge the gulf between the two "parallel universes" representing the separate worlds of Blacks and Whites in the twentieth century. Through his realistic and non-stereotyped depiction of human subjects, Commodore helped to end the "eight-ball" caricature

events.title: Meet Chester Commodore: Drawing and Illustration 101
events.description: Chester Commodore was one of the most influential and acclaimed African American cartoonists of the twentieth century. During the nearly 50 years his cartoons appeared in the Chicago Defender, Commodore used his art to advocate for racial justice, human rights, and equality of opportunity. From the 1954 appearance of his world-famous first editorial cartoon (on the Supreme Court’s Brown v. Board of Education, featuring a hammer breaking chains); his work reached an international audience. More than that, his widely seen cartoons helped to bridge the gulf between the two "parallel universes" representing the separate worlds of Blacks and Whites in the twentieth century. Through his realistic and non-stereotyped depiction of human subjects, Commodore helped to end the "eight-ball" caricature

events.title: Youth Safety & AI: A Facilitated Discussion
events.description: Disclaimer: This conversation will cover sensitive topics such as self-harm and suicide. This presentation is not suitable for minors. Last year, several teenagers tragically took their lives after extended conversations with AI chatbots that - rather than intervening - encouraged suicidal ideation and even suggested methods of self-harm. The families sued the companies, and although the lawsuits are ongoing, the chatbots are still available to the public today. Join us for a short video and discussion to explore the following questions: How did this happen? What safety measures are in place? What does it mean when AI malfunctions affect the most vulnerable? events.title: November Adult Book Discussion: My Friends by Fredrik Backman
events.description: Join us in November to discuss My Friends , a novel by Fredrik Backman. My Friends follows a fictional painting, The One of the Sea, a highly sought-after piece of art known for being the first work done by C. Jat, a world-famous artist. What many don’t see, however, is that it is not really a painting of the sea, or a beautiful landscape. Instead, it is a painting of three friends, standing out on the pier, with the artist all around them. Backman’s newest novel follows 18-year-old Louisa as she learns the story behind the painting, the people in it, and through their lives, finds herself along the way. events.title: When Studs Terkel Interviewed Me: What I Learned from Being Interviewed by the Pulitzer Prize-Winning Master Conversationalist
events.description: Before becoming an oral historian himself, Mark Larson had the unique experience of being interviewed twice by Studs Terkel, once for Race (under the pseudonym Peter Soderstrom) and later for Hope Dies Last . Larson also sat with Terkel in the WFMT studio as Terkel conducted a live interview for his radio program. Drawing on these encounters, Larson recalls what it felt like to be Terkel's interviewee and what it was like to watch one of America's great listeners at work. He reflects on what Terkel taught him about asking questions and truly listening for what's underneath the answers, and how those experiences inspired his own work in oral history. events.description: Join us in October to discuss the 2026 One Book, One Chicago Selection, Orbital by Samantha Harvey Orbital deftly snapshots one day in the lives of six women and men traveling through space. Writers of personal narrative use a metaphorical shovel, brush and precision instruments to dig around in territory of unreliable memory, searching for truths often lodged far below the surface.
